title: MJF-001 — Object storage client with magic-byte validation and AV scanning
body:
**MJF-001**

## Problem

There is no object-storage layer. CV uploads cannot be accepted at all, and the upload endpoint is the single highest-risk input in the product: it accepts arbitrary binary documents from the internet.

## Business impact

No CV upload means no product. Every downstream feature depends on it.

## Technical impact

Needs an S3-compatible client, streaming size enforcement, content-type verification by magic bytes rather than extension or client-supplied MIME, per-tenant opaque key namespacing, presigned download URLs, and an orphaned-object reaper for uploads never committed.

## Proposed solution

Implement internal/platform/storage over minio-go. Verify type by sniffing the first bytes, enforce the size cap during the stream so an oversized file is rejected mid-transfer rather than after being buffered, namespace keys under tenants/{user_id}/{uuid}, and issue short-TTL presigned URLs so the application is never on the bytes path. Add a ClamAV client and quarantine on a positive result.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Only PDF and DOCX are accepted, verified by magic bytes; a .pdf-named ZIP is rejected
- [ ] A file over STORAGE_MAX_CV_BYTES is rejected during transfer, not after
- [ ] Keys are opaque UUIDs under a per-tenant prefix; no filename is used in the key
- [ ] Download URLs are presigned with a TTL of 5 minutes or less
- [ ] An AV-positive file is quarantined, the candidate is notified, and the object is deleted after retention
- [ ] The bucket is created on first use so no broad storage credentials are needed in the app

## Testing requirements

Unit tests for magic-byte detection across valid PDF/DOCX and hostile inputs (polyglot, ZIP renamed, empty, truncated). Integration test against MinIO covering upload, presign, download and delete.

title: MJF-002 — CV upload endpoint and cv_documents/cv_versions persistence
body:
**MJF-002**

## Problem

No endpoint exists to accept a CV. The schema is ready but nothing writes to it.

## Business impact

Step 4 of the primary onboarding journey. A candidate cannot proceed without it.

## Technical impact

Multipart upload, a transaction creating the document and its first version, publishing cv.uploaded, and returning immediately with a parsing status so the client can poll.

## Proposed solution

POST /v1/cvs accepting multipart, streamed through the storage layer. Create cv_documents plus cv_versions(version_no=1) in one transaction, then publish cv.uploaded after commit. Enforce the cv_slots quota before accepting the body.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Upload returns 202 with a document id and parse_status=pending
- [ ] The cv_slots entitlement is checked before the body is read, not after the file is stored
- [ ] cv.uploaded carries cv_id, version_id, user_id, storage_key, content_type, size and checksum
- [ ] A storage failure leaves no database row
- [ ] Re-uploading the same file content creates a new version, not a duplicate document

## Testing requirements

API tests for success, oversized, wrong type, quota exceeded and storage-unavailable. Verify no orphaned rows after an induced storage failure.

title: MJF-003 — Deterministic text extraction from PDF and DOCX
body:
**MJF-003**

## Problem

A CV must be converted to text before anything can parse it. Sending a PDF straight to an LLM wastes tokens and loses layout information we can extract reliably and for free.

## Business impact

Parse quality determines match quality, which determines whether the product works at all.

## Technical impact

PDF text extraction plus DOCX XML extraction, with page and character counts. Must detect the image-only PDF case explicitly.

## Proposed solution

Implement extraction in the cv worker. For PDF use a pure-Go extractor; for DOCX read word/document.xml. Record char_count and page_count on the version. If char_count is zero, emit cv.parse_failed with reason=no_extractable_text and a clear candidate-facing message.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Text, page count and character count are persisted on the cv_version
- [ ] A scanned image-only PDF produces an explicit, actionable failure rather than an empty profile
- [ ] An encrypted or password-protected PDF is rejected with a clear message
- [ ] Extraction completes within 30 seconds for a 10-page CV
- [ ] CV text never appears in any log line

## Testing requirements

Fixture corpus: text PDF, scanned PDF, encrypted PDF, DOCX, DOCX with tables, malformed file, 50-page document. Assert the failure reason for each bad case.

title: MJF-004 — Provider-agnostic AI client with structured output, retries and token accounting
body:
**MJF-004**

## Problem

Every AI feature needs a shared client. Without one, each feature would reimplement schema validation, retries, timeouts and cost tracking, and they would diverge.

## Business impact

AI is the product's core differentiator and its largest variable cost. Untracked spend is an unbounded liability.

## Technical impact

Needs a provider interface, schema-constrained generation, bounded retries with a repair prompt on schema violation, per-call timeouts, output token caps, token accounting per purpose, and a prompt-injection-safe message construction helper.

## Proposed solution

Implement internal/platform/ai with a Provider interface, an Anthropic implementation defaulting to the current Claude models, and a Generate[T] helper that validates against a JSON schema and retries at most twice with a repair prompt. Untrusted text is passed only through a delimited data block helper that cannot be bypassed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No domain package imports a provider SDK directly
- [ ] A schema violation retries twice with a repair prompt, then returns a terminal error
- [ ] prompt_tokens, completion_tokens and total_tokens are recorded per call, labelled by purpose
- [ ] The ai_tokens_month quota is enforced before the call
- [ ] Prompt and completion bodies are never logged
- [ ] Untrusted text can only be included via the delimited-data helper

## Testing requirements

Unit tests with a fake provider: valid response, schema violation then recovery, schema violation exhausted, timeout, rate limit. A test asserting an injection string inside the data block does not alter the instruction portion.

title: MJF-005 — Structured CV extraction with per-field confidence and source offsets
body:
**MJF-005**

## Problem

Extracted text is unusable for matching until it is structured into experience, education, skills and certifications.

## Business impact

Match quality depends entirely on extraction quality. A wrongly parsed CV produces irrelevant matches and the candidate blames the product.

## Technical impact

Schema-constrained LLM extraction into cv_parsed_data, with a confidence score and a character offset per field so the UI can show provenance.

## Proposed solution

Define a strict extraction schema. Chunk long CVs. Persist per-field confidence and offsets in the confidence column. Surface low-confidence fields for candidate review rather than trusting them silently. Candidate corrections are recorded in corrected_fields and are never overwritten by a re-parse.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Experience, education, skills, certifications and languages are extracted into the documented schema
- [ ] Every field carries a confidence score and a character offset into the source text
- [ ] Fields below the confidence threshold are flagged for review
- [ ] A re-parse never overwrites a field listed in corrected_fields
- [ ] total_experience_months and detected_seniority are derived and stored
- [ ] An injection string in the CV does not alter the extraction instructions

## Testing requirements

A labelled corpus of at least 20 real-shaped CVs with expected extractions, asserting a minimum field-level accuracy. Adversarial CVs containing prompt-injection text.

title: MJF-006 — Skill normalisation against a canonical taxonomy
body:
**MJF-006**

## Problem

Raw skill strings are not comparable. 'JS', 'Javascript' and 'JavaScript' would be treated as three unrelated skills, making skill-overlap scoring meaningless.

## Business impact

Skill overlap is one of the heaviest match dimensions. If it is noise, matching is noise.

## Technical impact

Map extracted labels onto the skills table via canonical name, aliases and trigram similarity, persisting cv_skills with the raw label retained.

## Proposed solution

Seed the taxonomy with a substantial skill set and alias list. Normalise by exact match, then alias, then trigram similarity above a threshold. Retain the raw label so nothing is lost, and leave skill_id null rather than forcing a bad match.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Common aliases resolve to one canonical skill
- [ ] An unrecognised skill is retained with a null skill_id rather than force-matched
- [ ] The raw label is always preserved
- [ ] Normalisation is deterministic for a given input

## Testing requirements

A table test of alias resolution, including near-misses that must NOT match (e.g. 'Java' must not resolve to 'JavaScript').

title: MJF-007 — CV parse worker pipeline with idempotency and dead-lettering
body:
**MJF-007**

## Problem

The parse pipeline described in docs/SYSTEM_WORKFLOWS.md W1 has no consumers. Uploaded CVs would stay in pending forever.

## Business impact

A CV that never parses is a candidate who cannot use the product, with no explanation.

## Technical impact

Chained consumers: av-scan, text-extract, structure, skill-normalise, embed. Each idempotent, with the documented AckWait, MaxDeliver and timeouts.

## Proposed solution

Register the consumers in internal/worker under the cv group. Idempotency key cv.parse:{cv_version_id}. InFlightRetry throughout, since re-parsing is harmless. Publish cv.parsed on success and cv.parse_failed with the stage on terminal failure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All five stages run in order and are individually idempotent
- [ ] A redelivery after a crash does not duplicate derived rows
- [ ] A terminal failure dead-letters with the stage recorded and notifies the candidate
- [ ] Dead-letter depth above zero raises an alert
- [ ] The whole chain appears as one OpenTelemetry trace

## Testing requirements

Integration test against real Postgres, NATS and MinIO: upload to parsed, crash-and-resume mid-pipeline, and a poison message reaching the dead-letter queue.

title: MJF-008 — AI CV checker with deterministic rules plus an LLM pass
body:
**MJF-008**

## Problem

Candidates need concrete, actionable feedback on their CV. Generic advice is worthless and an opaque score is worse.

## Business impact

A free-tier acquisition feature and a genuine differentiator, but only if the advice is specific.

## Technical impact

Deterministic checks (length, sections present, contact detectable, date-format consistency, bullet density, ATS-parseability) combined with an LLM pass for impact and keyword coverage, feeding one documented scoring rubric.

## Proposed solution

Implement the rule layer first so a score exists without the AI. Add the LLM pass for impact and missing keywords. Every recommendation is anchored to a specific location in the CV. Cache by version hash plus target role.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The same CV always produces the same score
- [ ] Sub-scores are reported per category, not just an overall number
- [ ] Every recommendation names a specific location in the CV
- [ ] With the AI provider down, the deterministic subset is returned and the response states what is missing
- [ ] A fabricated score is never returned

## Testing requirements

Rubric unit tests per category. A snapshot test proving determinism. A degraded-mode test asserting the response declares its own incompleteness.

title: MJF-009 — Embeddings with a lexical fallback
body:
**MJF-009**

## Problem

Semantic title and skill matching needs embeddings, and matching must keep working when the embedding provider does not.

## Business impact

Semantic matching is what makes a 'Go developer' CV match a 'Backend Engineer (Golang)' posting.

## Technical impact

Generate title, skills and summary embeddings per CV version; store in cv_embeddings; provide cosine similarity and a lexical fallback.

## Proposed solution

Add an Embedder to the AI platform package. Persist vectors with their model and dimensions so a model change is detectable. When unavailable, fall back to trigram/token similarity and mark affected matches scoring_mode=degraded for later rescoring.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Embeddings are generated for each CV version and stored with model and dims
- [ ] Cosine similarity is correct against known vectors
- [ ] With the provider down, matching continues lexically and matches are marked degraded
- [ ] Degraded matches are rescored when the provider recovers
- [ ] A match is never dropped because scoring was degraded

## Testing requirements

Unit tests for cosine similarity and the fallback. An integration test forcing provider failure and asserting matches are still produced and marked.

## Problem

Implement the CRUD endpoints with user_id scoping. Soft-delete only; refuse hard deletion of a version referenced by any application and explain why.

- [ ] A candidate sees only their own CVs
- [ ] At most one default CV per candidate, enforced by the existing partial unique index
- [ ] A version used by a submitted application cannot be deleted
- [ ] Version history is preserved and browsable

Tenant-isolation test asserting another user's CVs are invisible and unmodifiable. A test proving a referenced version resists deletion.

title: MJF-011 — CV tailoring with mandatory factual containment validation
body:
**MJF-011**

## Problem

Tailoring is the highest-value AI feature and the highest-risk: an LLM asked to improve a CV for a job will invent experience unless actively prevented.

## Business impact

A fabricated line on a CV is a lie told in the candidate's name to an employer. It can cost them the role and their reputation. This is the product's most serious safety requirement.

## Technical impact

Generate a tailored version constrained to the parsed CV as the sole factual source, then run a post-generation validator that diffs against the source and rejects any new employer, title, date, certification or skill.

## Proposed solution

Implement the containment validator as a hard gate, independent of the prompt. Prompt compliance is necessary but insufficient, and a job description can carry an injection requesting exactly the fabrication we forbid. On rejection, retry once with a stricter prompt, then report that tailoring could not be completed safely. Persist containment_passed; the schema already requires it to be non-null for a tailored version.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Output introducing any employer, title, date, certification or skill absent from the source is rejected
- [ ] Unvalidated output is never surfaced to the candidate or attached to an application
- [ ] The candidate sees a diff against the source before the tailored CV is used
- [ ] containment_passed is recorded on every tailored version
- [ ] A prompt-injection attempt in the job description cannot defeat the validator

## Testing requirements

Adversarial suite: job descriptions demanding skills the candidate lacks; descriptions containing explicit injection instructions; a mocked provider returning fabricated content, asserting rejection. This suite is a release gate.

title: MJF-012 — CV builder with a sandboxed, network-isolated PDF renderer
body:
**MJF-012**

## Problem

Candidates need to create or restructure a CV in the product, and rendering user content to PDF is an SSRF and local-file-inclusion risk.

## Business impact

Removes the dependency on external CV tools and makes ATS-parseable output the default.

## Technical impact

Template registry, server-side HTML-to-PDF rendering, a preview that uses the same renderer as the final output.

## Proposed solution

Render in a sandboxed container with no network egress and no filesystem access beyond bundled fonts. Allowlist templates strictly. Use one renderer for both preview and output so what is previewed is what is produced.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Output is real text, single column by default, and ATS-parseable
- [ ] The renderer has no network access and cannot read local files
- [ ] Only allowlisted templates can be rendered
- [ ] Preview and final PDF are byte-identical for the same input
- [ ] A renderer timeout returns a clear failure, never a corrupt PDF

## Testing requirements

SSRF attempt tests (remote image, remote CSS, file:// reference) asserting each is blocked. A determinism test. An ATS-parseability check extracting text back out of the generated PDF.

title: MJF-020 — Adapter contract, registry and per-source circuit breaker
body:
**MJF-020**

## Problem

There is no abstraction over job sources. Without one, each integration would hand-roll its own rate limiting and failure handling and a single bad source could stall all discovery.

## Business impact

Job supply is the product's raw material. One failing board must not stop the others.

## Technical impact

The Adapter interface from docs/INTEGRATION_ANALYSIS.md, a registry, per-source rate limiting enforced inside the adapter, a persisted circuit breaker, and capability declaration.

## Proposed solution

Implement internal/domain/jobs/adapter with the documented interface. Capabilities drive planner behaviour so an unsupported query is skipped rather than issued and failed. Breaker state persists on job_sources so a restart does not immediately hammer a failing source.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every adapter implements Slug, Capabilities, Search, Fetch and HealthCheck
- [ ] Rate limiting is enforced inside the adapter so a scheduling bug cannot cause abuse
- [ ] A failing source degrades a run and never fails it
- [ ] Repeated failure opens the breaker, alerts, and persists across restart
- [ ] A source cannot be enabled without a recorded legal_basis

## Testing requirements

A shared conformance suite every adapter must pass. Breaker tests for open, half-open and close transitions.

title: MJF-024 — Discovery scheduler keyed by search specification
body:
**MJF-024**

## Problem

Discovery must run daily per loop, but running it per candidate would multiply upstream API cost by the number of candidates searching for the same thing.

## Business impact

Upstream rate limits and costs are the binding constraint on how many candidates the platform can serve.

## Technical impact

Resolve distinct search specs across all active loops, distribute runs across the day, hold a distributed lock per spec and source, and persist resumable cursors on discovery_runs.

## Proposed solution

Implement the scheduler binary with Redis leader election. Plan by spec hash, not by candidate, so N candidates searching identically cost one upstream query. Spread runs to smooth load and respect upstream limits.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two loops with identical specs produce one upstream query
- [ ] Only one scheduler instance plans at a time, via a Redis leader lock
- [ ] A worker crash resumes a run from its cursor rather than restarting it
- [ ] Runs are distributed across the day rather than bursting
- [ ] Every run records start, end, counts and errors, visible in the admin UI

## Testing requirements

Integration test with two identical loops asserting a single fetch. Crash-and-resume test. Leader-election test with two schedulers.

title: MJF-026 — Fingerprint deduplication with near-duplicate linking
body:
**MJF-026**

## Problem

The same job appears on many boards. Collapsing them wrongly merges distinct jobs; not collapsing them floods the candidate with duplicates.

## Business impact

Duplicate matches make the product feel broken. A wrongly merged pair silently hides a real opportunity.

## Technical impact

A deterministic fingerprint over normalised company, normalised title, geo key and a shingled description hash. Exact collision attaches a source attribution; near matches are linked, never merged.

## Proposed solution

Implement fingerprinting and the dedupe path. On exact fingerprint match, add a job_posting_sources row to the existing posting. On near match above the similarity threshold, insert both and link them as near_duplicate — merging two distinct jobs is unrecoverable, a link is cheap and reversible.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The same posting from three boards yields one job_postings row with three attributions
- [ ] Near-duplicates are linked with a similarity score, not merged
- [ ] The fingerprint is deterministic for identical input
- [ ] jobs.normalised is published only when content actually changed
- [ ] The UI can show 'also on Indeed, LinkedIn' from the attributions

## Testing requirements

A corpus of known duplicate and near-duplicate pairs with expected outcomes, including hard negatives that must not collapse.

- [ ] A submitted application is NOT retroactively changed
- [ ] The re-check respects per-source rate limits

title: MJF-028 — Loops domain: wizard, lifecycle with pause, and config versioning
body:
**MJF-028**

## Problem

Loops are the product's central abstraction and nothing implements them.

## Business impact

Without loops there is no automated search. Pause is the specific defect we identified in LoopCV and must not reproduce.

## Technical impact

Four-step resumable wizard, draft persistence, the draft/active/paused/archived state machine, config versioning, and a Redis kill-flag so pause takes effect in under a second.

## Proposed solution

Implement the loops domain. Pause sets a Redis flag that submission workers check immediately before every send, so pausing is near-instant rather than effective at the next scheduler tick. Every config change bumps config_version and snapshots the config, so a historical match can be explained by the settings in force when it was created.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The wizard is resumable; a partial loop persists as draft
- [ ] Pause halts discovery and pending submissions within one second
- [ ] Editing an active loop takes effect from the next run and is recorded as a config version
- [ ] Duplicating copies configuration but no history
- [ ] Preconditions are enforced at the step where they apply, not at submit
- [ ] The active_loops entitlement is enforced

## Testing requirements

State-machine tests for every transition including illegal ones. A race test pausing a loop while a submission is in flight, asserting the pre-send gate catches it.

- [ ] Required keywords are OR semantics; excluded keywords are any-match
- [ ] Company exclusion matches 'Acme, Inc.' and 'Acme Inc' alike

body:
**MJF-031**

## Problem

Matching is the product's core intelligence, and an unexplainable score is a support ticket. LoopCV's opaque Low/Middle/High knob is the defect we are replacing.

## Business impact

Candidates act on these scores. If they cannot see why a job scored 82, they cannot trust or tune the system.

Independent dimension scores — title similarity, required and nice-to-have skill overlap, years of experience, seniority fit, location fit, employment type fit — combined with versioned weights, producing per-dimension sub-scores and human-readable reasons.

## Proposed solution

Implement scoring with each dimension independently testable. Build the reason text from the structured sub-scores rather than from free-form LLM output, so an explanation cannot leak prompt content. Weights live in versioned config so historical scores stay interpretable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every match carries per-dimension sub-scores and reasons
- [ ] The numeric threshold plus the low/middle/high presets both work and agree
- [ ] Weights are versioned; config_version is recorded on each match
- [ ] Scoring is deterministic for identical inputs
- [ ] Explanation text is generated from structured data, never raw model output
- [ ] Degraded scoring is marked and rescored later, never dropped

Per-dimension unit tests. A golden-set regression suite of CV/posting pairs with expected score ranges, acting as a guard against scoring drift.

**MJF-042**

- [ ] Every authorisation stores a snapshot of exactly what was agreed
- [ ] Revocation takes effect before the next send
- [ ] Every grant and revocation is audited
- [ ] A submission completing just after a pause is recorded as authorised_before_pause

title: MJF-043 — Submission adapters with idempotency and honest outcome reporting
body:
**MJF-043**

## Problem

Submission is where an error becomes irreversible. A duplicate application cannot be recalled.

## Business impact

Applying twice to one job damages the candidate's standing with that employer.

## Technical impact

Submitters per method, an idempotency key persisted before dispatch, bounded retries for transient failures, and a first-class outcome_unknown state when a request was sent but the response was lost.

## Proposed solution

Implement the Submitter contract with the key written before dispatch and completed after. On redelivery with a key in_flight, report outcome_unknown and dead-letter rather than repeating a possibly-successful send. Never auto-retry an unknown outcome.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Submit is safe to call twice with the same idempotency key
- [ ] A lost response produces outcome_unknown, never a guess or a silent retry
- [ ] Transient failures retry with backoff up to a cap, then fail with a reason
- [ ] Permanent failures are terminal with a reason
- [ ] Per-destination-domain rate limits are enforced
- [ ] The pre-send gate re-checks authorisation, cap, pause flag, suppression and cooldown

## Testing requirements

Idempotency tests per method. A simulated lost-response test asserting outcome_unknown and no retry. A concurrency test with two workers on one application asserting a single submission.

title: MJF-061 — Outreach sending with suppression, SMTP support and bounce handling
body:
**MJF-061**

## Problem

Sending application emails without suppression and bounce handling destroys deliverability for every candidate on the platform.

## Business impact

One candidate's spam complaints must not poison delivery for everyone else.

## Technical impact

Platform sending with the candidate in Reply-To, optional candidate SMTP with envelope-encrypted credentials, per-recipient-domain rate limits, global suppression checked before every send, and bounce and complaint handling.

## Proposed solution

Implement the send path with the suppression check as an unconditional pre-send gate. SMTP credentials are write-only through the API, never returned and never logged. Hard bounces suppress permanently; complaints suppress and alert.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The suppression list is checked before every send without exception
- [ ] SMTP credentials are never returned by any endpoint and never appear in logs
- [ ] Per-recipient-domain rate limits are enforced
- [ ] A hard bounce suppresses permanently; a complaint suppresses and alerts

title: MJF-065 — Subscriptions, entitlements and webhook-authoritative billing
body:
**MJF-065**

## Problem

Entitlements are defined in the plans table but nothing enforces them, and there is no billing integration.

## Business impact

No revenue, and no protection against a single user consuming unbounded AI spend.

## Technical impact

Stripe checkout, signature-verified idempotent webhooks as the source of truth, entitlement resolution, Redis quota counters with a nightly Postgres reconciliation, and graceful degradation at the limit.

## Proposed solution

Implement entitlements.Check as the single enforcement point. Webhooks are keyed on the provider's event id because providers deliver duplicates and out-of-order events routinely. Exceeding a quota degrades gracefully: matches keep accumulating and submissions queue rather than fail.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Quotas are enforced server-side only; a client-supplied tier is never trusted
- [ ] Webhook signatures are verified and processing is idempotent on the provider event id
- [ ] Out-of-order webhooks do not corrupt subscription state
- [ ] A lost webhook is caught by nightly reconciliation
- [ ] Exceeding a quota queues submissions rather than losing them
- [ ] A Redis outage falls back to the Postgres rollup with a conservative cap

## Testing requirements

Webhook replay, duplicate and out-of-order tests. Quota boundary tests. A Redis-failure test asserting the conservative fallback.

title: MJF-066 — GDPR data export and account erasure
body:
**MJF-066**

## Problem

There is no way for a candidate to export or erase their data, which is a legal obligation for a platform holding CVs and application history.

## Business impact

A non-negotiable legal requirement, and a trust signal.

## Technical impact

An export job assembling per-table JSON plus original CV files; a 7-day grace period; an idempotent resumable erasure job with a verification pass.

## Proposed solution

Implement both as resumable idempotent jobs. Deletion halts automation immediately while leaving sign-in available during the grace period, so a candidate can cancel. The erasure verification pass fails loudly rather than reporting a partial erasure as complete.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Export covers every table holding the candidate's data plus their CV files
- [ ] Export links are single-use with a one-hour TTL and bound to the requesting session
- [ ] Automation halts immediately on a deletion request; sign-in continues during grace
- [ ] Erasure is resumable and idempotent
- [ ] A verification pass confirms completeness and fails loudly if not
- [ ] Deletion is available on every tier

## Testing requirements

An export completeness test enumerating every table with a user_id column. An erasure test asserting the verification pass catches an induced partial erasure.
